draft.title: Cohesion through pronouns and word chains
card: Cohesion means the sentences in a text link together so it reads as one connected whole, not a set of separate lines.
a word such as he, she, it, they or this that refers back to something already named. If a text says Priya found a map and then says she studied it, she means Priya and it means the map.
a string of related words through a text, such as sailor, ship, deck, ocean. The repeated topic keeps the reader on one subject.
A pronoun should clearly match one earlier noun. If it could mean two things, the reader may be confused.
draft.remember: Pronouns and word chains tie sentences together so the text flows as one.

a.q: Tom lost his torch in the cave. A second sentence says it was never found. What does the pronoun it refer back to?
a.why: It refers back to the torch, the thing that was lost and could be found. The cave is tempting because it is also a noun in the first sentence, but a cave is not usually something that is lost.
a.clue: What was lost and could be found?

b.q: A paragraph uses the words coach, training, drills, laps and team. What is this an example of?
opts: A word chain that keeps the text on one topic
A pronoun that refers back to a noun
A pronoun that sets up a new topic
A word chain that shifts topic each sentence
b.why: The words are all related to sport training, so they form a word chain that holds the topic together. None of them is a pronoun, because none stands in for an earlier noun.
b.clue: The words are all related in meaning.

b.best: A word chain that keeps the text on one topic
